mcqs.q: Which attachment style was most prevalent among the commercial-breeding-kennel dogs tested?
mcqs.e: Twenty of 48 dogs (41.67%) were classified secure, the largest group.

mcqs.q: Relative to insecure-avoidant dogs, how did secure and ambivalent dogs behave toward a stranger?
o: Approached and solicited contact more frequently
mcqs.e: Secure/ambivalent dogs approached and solicited contact significantly more than avoidant dogs.

mcqs.q: What effect did caretaker presence (Paired-Effect vs Stranger Arena) have on approach to the stranger?
o: Dogs approached the stranger faster when the caretaker was present
No dogs approached in either test
mcqs.e: All groups approached more quickly when the caretaker was present, a secure-base effect.

mcqs.q: How did owners of HSHA-affected dogs rate their own quality of life versus control owners?
mcqs.e: HSHA owners reported significantly lower QoL, citing stress, injuries, and emotional distress.

mcqs.q: Compared with controls, HSHA dogs showed:
o: Better welfare and fewer health issues
Lower well-being and more frequent physical health problems
mcqs.e: HSHA dogs had lower well-being plus more injuries and digestive problems.

mcqs.q: What did the authors emphasize as the key to improving HSHA outcomes?
mcqs.e: Early diagnosis/management was stressed to prevent relinquishment or euthanasia.

mcqs.q: What did free-ranging dogs demonstrate across the trial days?
o: No ability to distinguish the experimenters
Learning to identify the rewarding person
mcqs.e: Correct choices rose significantly by days 5 and 6 versus day 2, indicating learning.

mcqs.q: On which days were correct choices significantly higher than on Day 2?
mcqs.e: Dogs chose the previously rewarding person significantly more often on days 5 and 6.

mcqs.q: What reward marked the correct experimenter?
mcqs.e: The rewarding experimenter gave boiled chicken followed by petting.

mcqs.q: Which toy did shelter dogs engage with longest?
mcqs.e: Dogs engaged over eight times longer with the stuffed toy than other toys.

mcqs.q: What was the effect of applying a dog's preferred scent to its toys?
o: Increased engagement with both most- and least-preferred toys
mcqs.e: Scent boosted engagement, with the biggest gain (13.7x) on least-preferred toys.

mcqs.q: On average, what fraction of the 15-minute session did dogs spend interacting with toys?
mcqs.e: Dogs interacted with toys only 3.35% of the session on average.

mcqs.q: Did the MSWO preference test predict in-home toy engagement?
mcqs.e: MSWO did not predict in-home toy engagement.

mcqs.q: What happened to overall activity and play with increasing dog age?
mcqs.e: Overall activity and play declined with age.

mcqs.q: What was the practical conclusion about scent enrichment?
o: A single universal scent works best
Personalized, individual-preference scenting can enhance welfare
mcqs.e: No single scent was universally preferred; individualized preference raised activity, supporting personalized enrichment.

mcqs.q: Which sound did dogs actively avoid?
mcqs.e: Dogs avoided agonistic vocalizations and increased owner attention-seeking.

mcqs.q: What effect did prior familiarity with classical music have?
o: Familiar dogs spent about twice as long in the sound zone and were more relaxed
mcqs.e: Prior-exposure dogs spent twice as much time in the sound zone and showed more relaxed behaviors.

mcqs.q: Did any supposedly 'positive' stimulus produce a clear preference?
mcqs.e: None of the positive stimuli produced a clear preference; dogs may even prefer silence.

mcqs.q: Were there behavioral differences between fearful and control dogs during home separation?
o: Fearful dogs were much more distressed
No differences were found between fearful and control dogs
mcqs.e: No differences were found between fearful dogs and controls.

mcqs.q: Which change during the owner's absence was interpreted as a stress indicator?
o: Decreased exploration that did not fully recover
mcqs.e: Reduced exploration during absence, with incomplete recovery after return, indicated stress.

mcqs.q: What methodological contribution did the study make?
o: Showed separation can be evaluated in a naturalistic home setting
mcqs.e: It demonstrated separation reactions can be assessed in the dog's own home rather than a novel place.

mcqs.q: Which early-life factor was associated with LOWER odds of separation-related behaviour?
o: Sleeping >=9 h/night plus overnight crate/room confinement at <=16 weeks
mcqs.e: Puppies with >=9 h sleep and enclosed overnight space were less likely to develop SRBs.

mcqs.q: Owners who 'fussed' over puppies in response to bad behaviour on return had puppies that were:
o: About six times more likely to show SRBs
mcqs.e: Fussing was linked to roughly six-fold higher odds of SRBs.

mcqs.q: What was found for dog breed, sex, and source?
o: No significant association with SRB occurrence
mcqs.e: Breed, sex and source showed no significant association with SRB occurrence.

mcqs.q: Which training approach did shelter dogs respond best to?
mcqs.e: Dogs responded better to treats, verbal praise, and stroking than to clicker alone.

mcqs.q: Was the learned 'sit' retained after changing trainer or location?
mcqs.e: The 'sit' was retained even after a change of location and/or trainer.

mcqs.q: What outcome do the authors link to teaching basic obedience in shelters?
mcqs.e: Basic obedience is a desirable trait that can increase adoptability.

mcqs.q: In the Dog Aging Project sample, what proportion of dogs met the threshold for at least one (or >=2) moderate-to-serious behavior problems?
mcqs.e: 99.12% of dogs met the threshold for at least one problem.

mcqs.q: Which behavior category had the HIGHEST prevalence (>=2 moderate-to-serious occurrences)?
mcqs.e: Separation/attachment behaviors were highest at 85.9%.

mcqs.q: Which behavior category had the LOWEST prevalence?
mcqs.e: Housesoiling was lowest at 4.1%.

mcqs.q: Did diffuser dog-appeasing pheromone produce significant stress-reducing cardiovascular changes in hospitalized dogs?
mcqs.e: DAP produced no significant or clinically relevant cardiovascular stress-reduction effects.

mcqs.q: What did the placebo group's heart-rate pattern at arrival (T0) indicate?
o: Stress upon arrival in the hospital
mcqs.e: Heart-rate changes at baseline versus later timepoints suggested arrival stress.

mcqs.q: What study design was used?
mcqs.e: It was a prospective, paired, randomized, double-blinded study of ten dogs.

mcqs.q: Into which two personality groups were the dogs classified?
mcqs.e: Dogs were assigned to introvert or extrovert groups.

mcqs.q: What proportion of the 46 dogs were assessed as extroverts?
mcqs.e: 28 of 46 dogs (61%) showed extrovert traits; 18 (39%) were introverts.

mcqs.q: Which statistical method built the temperament-assessment model?
o: Logistic regression on counts of extrovert/introvert traits
mcqs.e: Logistic regression used numbers of extrovert and introvert traits to predict a dichotomous temperament outcome.
